narrative:
The model estimated a 29% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, among applicants with a similar profile, about three in ten would be expected to have repayment difficulty. That estimate did not meet the approval standard used for this application, so the loan was denied.

The key upward pressure came from your existing bank installment plan. Only about 8.7% of approved applicants have this type of plan, and it was the second most influential factor overall but the main factor moving your application toward higher risk. The most influential factor was your checking-account profile showing no recorded balance; this worked in your favor and is also the most common pattern among approved applicants. The third factor, your requested repayment period of 12 months, was shorter than the approved average of about 19 months and modestly reduced your risk. These favorable points helped, but not enough to offset the concern about your existing bank installment commitment.

To improve your position, focus on reducing existing installment obligations, especially the bank plan, before reapplying. Avoid taking on new credit, keep account activity stable, and gather clear evidence of income and savings. Ask the lender what repayment or debt-reduction evidence would strengthen a future application.
